brief: The ticker is the town's one channel for saying what it is doing, and it loses the end of what it says. Re-shot on HEAD at 1600x950 during this manager pass: `A hatch goes back on the roof below the window and a basket of wash…` clipped mid-word. The slot is a fixed width and the 37 `sayAt` sentences are not (c295). Fix the SLOT, not the sentences — measure the rendered width of the whole corpus at the sizes the ticker is shown at, and make the layout hold the longest of them.
successLooksLike: At 1600x950, 1280x800 and 1024x700 no ticker line is cut mid-word — every one of the 37 sentences either fits its slot or is composed to fit it.
avoid: Do not shrink the ticker's type below the footer's other text, and do not solve it by hand-shortening the 37 sentences: the fix must hold for the next sentence somebody writes. The chrome is hidden under 640px, so the phone is not in scope here — it is b206's.
